Searched the pinned mathlib List, Computability and permutation sources, Lean core List lemmas, local primitives and the original paper for block-reversal/reflected-block facilities. Core List.reverse_flatten and reverse_reverse concern list values and do not provide a paid native tape schedule. The existing local BankReversal reverses individual bits and decodes symbols through Bool, so it is not a substitute for entry-preserving, trit-safe block reversal. Reused ScheduledAdvance rather than writing another right-seek implementation; reused ScheduledTransfer for reads/writes/source clearing and frame facts; reused ScheduledTapeAction rewinds, ScheduledNativeIO append, ScheduledWord/repeatSchedule, RepeatedScheduleMotion, and the exact-symbol BankWord interface. Mathlib/core Function.iterate_succ_apply and its primed form, Nat.div_lt_iff_lt_mul, Nat.div_add_mod', Nat.mod_lt, multiplication monotonicity and natural subtraction facts supply the algebraic chain. No new tape semantics, compiler, IO implementation or lower-bound machinery. This is implementation infrastructure for exact source206(a,b), not a new research impossibility theorem.
